quote: Not really interested right now, but I'll, if I do, I'll get with you.
stewart_read: This is squarely the hello-objection pattern — customer distancing within the opening moments. The script calls for an acknowledge-then-small-ask response.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep's actual response (build an estimate, no commitment) is a reasonable improvisation of the small-ask spirit, but it isn't the structured 30-second ask the protocol specifies.
coaching_implication: Coach the literal small-ask phrasing ('can I have 30 seconds...') so the rep has a repeatable move here instead of freelancing a value explanation.

quote: Give me a ballpark figure on what it cost.

alternative_hypothesis: Rep's tax-incentive answer is not wrong content, but it does not extract the roof/bill/address info the schema's canonical response is built to capture.

quote: There's not a very big house. I mean, it's, 2,000 square foot.
stewart_read: Customer volunteers a concrete home-size detail unprompted — a natural entry point to start the verify conversation (roof, bill, utility) and build toward a real estimate. Rep just says 'Okay' and lets the moment pass.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may have judged the call was ending soon (customer already signaling he's busy) and chose not to invest more time — but there is no evidence in the transcript that this was a deliberate strategic choice rather than a missed cue.
coaching_implication: Show the rep this exact line as a missed entry point — 'that's a great size to work with, mind if I grab your utility company and average bill while we're on the phone?' would have moved the call forward instead of stalling.

quote: Can I reach you back at this number?
stewart_read: This is the pivot point where the call needed a firm time anchor (protocols.time_constraint) and instead the rep let the customer set the terms of re-contact.
alternative_hypothesis: Given the customer stated a genuine plumbing emergency, deferring is situationally reasonable — but the rep still needed to lock a specific callback day/time rather than accept an open-ended 'reach you back.'
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to always convert 'call me back' into a specific day/time ask, even under real time pressure — 'Totally understand — how about I call you tomorrow at 2?'

coaching_implication: This is the clearest actionable gap on the call: rep needed to counter the vague 'in a week' with a specific date ('let's actually pencil in next Tuesday at 10 so it's on both our calendars') rather than accepting an open-ended promise.

coaching_implication: Flag for the security/privacy review the schema calls for, and coach the rep that texting personal info is not a substitute for locking a date.
